data.title: Ethnosport Cultural Festival Opens at Riyadh Season
data.content:
Riyadh, November 20, 2026, SPA -- The Ethnosport Cultural Festival opened yesterday evening at New Murabba in Riyadh, attended by General Entertainment Authority (GEA) Board of Directors Chairman Turki Alalshikh and World Ethnosport Union President Necmeddin Bilal Erdoğan, with more than 18 countries showcasing 38 traditional sports and games.
    The event marks the first edition of the festival to be held outside Türkiye, hosted by Riyadh Season. The opening ceremony was attended by a number of princes, senior officials, representatives of participating countries and sports federations, and festival guests from around the world.
    The ceremony began with an address by Alalshikh, who welcomed the distinguished guests and expressed his gratitude and appreciation to the Kingdom's leadership for its continued support of the entertainment sector and Riyadh Season.
    He expressed his pleasure at hosting the Ethnosport Cultural Festival for the first time outside Türkiye, describing it as an international event that brings people together and celebrates their sporting and cultural heritage.
    Alalshikh emphasized that Riyadh Season, now in its seventh edition, continues to attract international events and offer diverse experiences. He noted that since its launch in 2019, the season has consistently sought to diversify its offerings across various sectors. Hosting the festival represents a continuation of this approach, with more than 18 brotherly countries presenting 38 traditional sports and games in a celebration reflecting the richness of global heritage and cultural diversity.
    He also addressed the partnership with the World Ethnosport Union, explaining that cooperation between the two parties was announced in Istanbul in September and that hosting the festival in Riyadh now represents the tangible outcome of that collaboration in the Saudi capital.
    Alalshikh thanked Bilal Erdoğan for his efforts and cooperation, as well as the achievements accomplished within this short period. He expressed pride in the partnership between the two sides, which will continue next year through Riyadh Season's sponsorship of the festival's 2027 edition in Istanbul.
    He also expressed his hope that Riyadh's hosting of the event would mark the beginning of further cooperation with the World Ethnosport Union, contributing to raising awareness of traditional sports, preserving their heritage, and passing it on to future generations.
    For his part, Bilal Erdoğan expressed his pleasure at holding the Ethnosport Cultural Festival for the first time in Saudi Arabia as part of Riyadh Season and meeting participants and guests in the capital.
    Erdoğan emphasized that Saudi Arabia's hosting of the festival represents a new milestone in the World Ethnosport Union's journey, and that the union had long aspired to bring the Ethnosport Cultural Festival experience to different parts of the world after completing its eighth edition in Istanbul. He affirmed that hosting the festival in Riyadh fulfills one of those ambitions, made possible by the support and warm welcome the event has received in Saudi Arabia.
    Erdoğan noted that the World Ethnosport Union currently comprises 56 member organizations from 34 countries across five continents. Working alongside its members, the union seeks to revive, preserve, and pass traditional sports and games on to future generations, while bringing participants from different countries together in one arena to promote friendship, peace, and solidarity among peoples.
    He explained that the festival in Riyadh welcomes hundreds of participants from around the world to celebrate their cultural heritage and share their traditions with others. He emphasized that the activities have been designed to accommodate children, young people, women, and visitors of all ages through a program combining traditional sports and games, arts, handicrafts, and diverse cuisines, collectively representing aspects of humanity's shared heritage passed down through generations across different countries.
    He highlighted that bringing these cultures together in Riyadh offers participants and visitors an opportunity to hear the stories of different peoples and gain firsthand insight into their diverse traditions, stressing the importance of preserving cultural roots and the historical connections that unite communities.
    He stressed the importance of reconnecting with cultural roots, strengthening shared values among peoples, and reinforcing ties through respect, solidarity, peace, and the preservation of traditions. He praised the exceptional level of organization and generous hospitality he had experienced in Riyadh, describing them as evidence of the efforts made to ensure the festival's success.
    Erdoğan expressed his hope that the festival's 10 days would create unforgettable memories and experiences for participants and visitors. He affirmed his confidence that the cooperation between the two sides would contribute to delivering a historic event that brings together the world's traditions, sports, and diverse cultures in one location.
    He also expressed his hope that the Ethnosport Cultural Festival would strengthen the brotherly relations between Saudi Arabia and Türkiye and open new opportunities for cooperation between the two countries, supporting their shared objectives of preserving traditional sports and promoting their cultural significance.
    The opening ceremony also featured a major artistic and theatrical performance that began with the entrance of the participating delegations, led by representatives from the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Through a series of choreographed scenes, the performance celebrated the sporting and cultural heritage of different peoples, highlighting the history of traditional sports and the skills and artistic practices passed down through generations. Combining artistic performances with heritage elements, the show reflected the cultural diversity celebrated by the festival and received enthusiastic applause and admiration from guests and representatives of participating countries.
    Ahead of the opening ceremony, Alalshikh and Erdoğan toured the festival grounds to explore its facilities and various zones, as well as the sporting, cultural, and heritage experiences showcasing the traditional customs of participating countries.
    The Ethnosport Cultural Festival, which runs until November 28, offers an experience combining traditional sporting competitions, cultural performances, and folk arts. Hundreds of athletes, artists, and artisans from countries around the world are participating in the event, which aims to introduce visitors to the sporting and cultural heritage of different peoples and contribute to its preservation.
    Festival activities include various forms of traditional wrestling, equestrian sports, and archery, alongside folk and strategy games, handicraft workshops, and folkloric performances. Dedicated interactive areas for children and families also allow visitors to discover and participate in traditional sports.
    The festival welcomes visitors daily from 5 p.m. until midnight at New Murabba in Riyadh, with tickets available through webook. The event adds another international experience to Riyadh Season's program, bringing together sports, heritage, and culture in a single destination.
    -- SPA
